sections.title: Theoretical Results
sections.extract: Viewing routing as a one-step Bayesian decision problem, the Bayes-optimal expected utility is monotone in the conditioning σ-algebra. This is the classical “information never hurts” principle for Bayes decision rules (DeGroot, 1962; Blackwell, 1953), instantiated in our trajectory- conditioning setting. sections.title: Related Work
sections.extract: Building on agentic frameworks like ReAct (Yao et al., 2023), recent work equips LLMs to operate on real repositories. SWE-agent (Yang et al., 2024a;b) introduces an agent–computer interface for browsing, editing, and executing code. Code benchmarks have moved from self-contained problems (Chen et al., 2021; Austin et al., 2021; Hendrycks et al., 2021) to repository-level evaluation. SWE-bench (Jimenez et al., 2024)

sections.title: Conclusion
sections.extract: We introduced SWE-Router, a value-based routing framework that conditions on a short partial trajectory of a cheap weak model rather than on the task description alone. A simple Bayes-optimality result (Theorem 4.1) shows that this conditioning never harms routing and is strictly better when exploration is informative. sections.title: Impact Statement
sections.extract: Our approach provides a clear positive impact of reduced frontier-model inference cost and energy use with minimal tradeoff in the overall performance. However, our proposed approach of utilizing partial trajectories can be misused to bypass safety-focused frontier models for malicious pur- poses.
